bugs: Dashboard invalidation via Cache::forget is racy: a recompute already in flight when a change commits can write pre-change data back under the same key, which then stays for up to 5 minutes (app/Dashboard/TeamDashboard.php:26 with app/Observers/*Observer.php)
The lock wait is 5s, longer than the 3s 'slow' threshold, so on a cold miss waiting requests can take up to 5s before falling back (app/Exchange/ExchangeRates.php:23)
antipatterns: API routes are put in routes/web.php under Route::prefix('api') instead of routes/api.php with withRouting(api:) (routes/web.php:10-14)

The stampede test is misleading and slow: the nested call blocks 5s on the lock and then raises RatesUnavailableException, yet the test passes; it never shows the waiter getting fresh data (tests/Feature/ExchangeRatesTest.php:73-92)
Exception classes are split across App\Exceptions and App\Exchange for the same feature (app/Exchange/UnexpectedRatesResponse.php, app/Exceptions/RatesUnavailableException.php)
Uses Cache::remember instead of Cache::flexible, although the task explicitly allows serving stale data during a slow recompute (app/Dashboard/TeamDashboard.php:26)
Tests reset the HTTP fake with Http::swap(new Factory) instead of a sequence or closure fake (tests/Feature/ExchangeRatesTest.php:13-16)
strengths: Observers use ShouldHandleEventsAfterCommit and #[ObservedBy], so invalidation waits for commit; the old team_id/project_id is captured in saving, which handles moves
The RatesUnavailableException render() method keeps the controller to one line
The lock re-checks the cache inside the critical section, and a failure cooldown stops repeated calls to a failing API
Uses #[Scope] attributes, enum casts, withCount with a constrained alias, and a hasManyThrough for team tasks
Broad tests: membership changes, moves between teams, TTL fallback for raw writes, malformed payload, recovery

bugs: GET /api/exchange-rates/{currency} needs authentication (route group ['web','auth']), which the task did not ask for; a guest gets 401 (routes/api.php:7-10)
The lock wait is 5s, longer than the 3s 'slow' threshold, so on a cold miss waiters can take up to 5s before the stale/503 fallback (config/services.php lock_wait)
antipatterns: Cache-versioning logic (Cache and DB facades, afterCommit) lives on the Team Eloquent model instead of the dashboard action or service (app/Models/Team.php:35-64)
Applies the 'web' middleware group inside routes/api.php (routes/api.php:7)
The exchange-rates URL is hardcoded in config without env() (config/services.php rates.url)
Uses Cache::remember instead of Cache::flexible despite the stale-while-revalidate allowance (app/Actions/GetTeamDashboard.php:19)
Every dashboard request makes an extra cache read for the version key; this is ceremony compared with a plain forget
Task #[Fillable] includes completed_at but leaves out assignee_id (app/Models/Task.php:17)
strengths: Version-bump invalidation, deferred with DB::afterCommit, prevents a recompute already in flight from writing stale data back and skips rolled-back changes
Collects the old and new team ids with getOriginal in saved and deduplicates them with collect()->filter()->unique()
Clean action classes; the null-coalescing abort and the 503 mapping keep the controllers thin
Deterministic lock tests (lock_wait=0) and preventStrayRequests set globally in Pest.php; dataset-driven failure tests for server error and timeout
HTTP failures are handled without exceptions as control flow (successful() check and ConnectionException), plus a failure backoff

v.rationale: Both implementations are close and pass their suites. Both use remember (not flexible), per-team keys, model observers, a lock with a re-check inside it, a failure cooldown, a forever or 30-day last-known copy, and a 3s timeout. impl-2's version-bump invalidation after commit is more robust than impl-1's plain forget, which can be undone by a recompute already in flight. impl-2's tests are also more deterministic and faster; impl-1's stampede test is misleading and takes 5s. Against that, impl-2 puts the exchange-rate endpoint behind auth without being asked and keeps cache logic on the Team model. impl-1 puts API routes in web.php. Weighing these, impl-2 wins narrowly.
